name: Moby-Dick
hook: A whaling novel with a famous first line and a white whale Jeopardy never stops chasing.

facts.label: Herman Melville
facts.statement: Herman Melville published it in 1851 after shipping out as a sailor; his other fiction includes Typee, Billy Budd and "Bartleby, the Scrivener".

facts.label: Ishmael
facts.statement: The novel opens "Call me Ishmael." Ishmael is the narrator, and at the end the Pequod sinks while he is the lone survivor.

facts.label: Ahab
facts.statement: Captain Ahab, named for an evil king of Israel, commands the Pequod and hunts the white whale that took his leg.

facts.label: the sperm whale
facts.statement: Moby Dick is an albino sperm whale, the largest of the toothed whales — and Connecticut's state animal.

facts.label: the Pequod
facts.statement: The Pequod is Ahab's ship, named for a New England tribe destroyed by the Puritans; it sinks at the novel's end.

facts.label: the white whale in later works
facts.statement: Later writers kept the whale: Jules Verne mentions Moby Dick in a novel, Ray Bradbury wrote the screenplay, and Jaws was called a mix of it and Ibsen.
